key_insight: SciExam for ENSO introduces a real-world benchmark that tests whether AI agents can build scientifically valid climate models, not just produce answers that look correct. It evaluates agents on constructing low-order stochastic models of ENSO directly from observations within a constrained time budget.
problem_solved: Traditional AI benchmarks for scientific tasks usually compare outputs to known answers, rubrics, or model-based reviewers, which cannot verify whether a newly generated scientific model is genuinely valid. This paper addresses the need for an evaluation setting that measures whether AI agents can discover and build useful physical models from data.
method: Defines the SciExam for ENSO benchmark, where agents must infer low-order stochastic models of the El Niño-Southern Oscillation from real observational data.
Uses a six-hour time-limited challenge to test open-ended scientific modeling ability under realistic constraints.
Evaluates agent performance based on the quality and scientific validity of the resulting climate model rather than simple answer matching.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this paper points toward more meaningful evaluation of agentic research systems in scientific discovery settings. It helps shift benchmark design from surface-level correctness toward true model-building capability and physical validity.
